title: Lights Out
rule: It can only move in the dark.
logline: When a blackout hits the city, a girl who has been scared of the dark her whole life discovers the giant in the street can only move when the lights are off — and that its own shadow counts.
thumb_text: IT ONLY MOVES IN THE DARK
hook_caption: It only moves in the dark. Then the generator started dying… 🔦
description: A blackout. A giant in the street. One rule: it can only move in the dark. Mia has been scared of the dark her whole life — tonight that fear is the only thing that can save the city.

mia.name: Mia
mia.bio: 14. Has slept with a lamp on every night of her life and carries a flashlight everywhere. Want: get home. Flaw: afraid of the dark — which turns out to be expertise.

reyes.name: Officer Reyes
reyes.bio: Runs the barricade. Trusts procedure until procedure runs out of fuel.

monster.name: The Dimwalker
monster.bio: A 56 m stone colossus with ice-blue fissures. Statue-still in any light; the instant a patch of it is in darkness, that part can move.
monster.signature: one huge step per heartbeat of darkness; a low grinding roar; ground-cracking stomps

premises.premise: A blackout city; the giant can only move in the dark; a girl afraid of the dark keeps it lit.
It freezes whenever anyone looks at it; a night-shift guard must not blink.
It can only step when the clock tower strikes; eleven strikes left.
It can only see heat; a boy hides the whole street in a cold-storage depot.
It can't cross painted lines; a road crew paints the city into a cage.
It copies the nearest person's movements; a dancer leads it into the harbour.
It only hunts while the city is awake; a radio DJ must put a million people to sleep.
It comes to whoever says its name; a news anchor is live on air.
It grows every time someone screams; a fire drill turns into the worst idea ever.
It can only walk on concrete; the city has one park in its path.

why: Strongest hook + the most visual rule (light vs dark is readable without words), the hero's flaw becomes the solution, and the shadow loophole gives a reversal the audience can see coming one second before the characters do.
outline: Blackout ripples across the skyline; a giant takes a step in the dark.
Floodlights snap on; it freezes mid-stride. It only moves in the dark.
Mia, scared of the dark her whole life, flashlight in hand.
Generator dying; every flicker, it is closer (jump-scare cuts).
Its shadow: the hand behind its back is in darkness — it rips a floodlight down.
Mia: light it from everywhere. Cars ring it, beams up. No shadows.
Generator dies. Total dark. It lunges at Mia.
Mia does what she does every night: clicks on her flashlight — into its eye. Frozen.
Lights blaze. It never moves again; a park is built around it. Mia sleeps with the lights off.
draft:
NARRATOR: At 11:52 PM the power grid failed and the entire city was plunged into total darkness.
NARRATOR: Something enormous that had been hiding in the dark began to move.
NARRATOR: The police turned on their emergency floodlights and pointed them at the creature.
NARRATOR: Amazingly, it stopped moving the second the light hit it.
NARRATOR: Scientists would later learn the rule: it can only move in the dark.
NARRATOR: Mia was a fourteen-year-old girl who had always been afraid of the dark.
REYES: The generator is running out of fuel, we only have a few minutes left!
NARRATOR: Each flicker of the lights let it move closer.
MIA: Keep the lights on it!
NARRATOR: Then Mia noticed its shadow, and its hand was moving inside it.
REYES: It's moving in its own shadow!
MIA: We need to light it from every direction so there are no shadows.
NARRATOR: The plan worked for a while, but then the generator finally died.
NARRATOR: Mia turned on her flashlight and pointed it into the monster's eye.
NARRATOR: It froze. Then the police turned all their lights on and it never moved again.
NARRATOR: Today there is a park around it, and Mia isn't afraid of the dark anymore.
critique: Hook is 19 words — far too slow for a 2-second hook. Cut to the time stamp + the step.
'Scientists would later learn' breaks tension and is a flash-forward nobody needs. Show the rule, then say it in 7 words.
Mia's flaw is told, not shown — give her the flashlight in the first shot she appears in, so the payoff is planted.
The flicker escalation needs a visual rule the audience can track: each flicker = a jump cut, monster visibly closer.
The reversal (shadow) is great but explained flat — split into 'saw its shadow' / 'its hand was moving' for a beat of dread.
The ending tells us she's 'not afraid anymore' — too neat. Better button: she sleeps with the lights OFF (image, not statement).
No silence anywhere. Add a full music drop when the generator dies; let the dark sit for a second.
Win is a cheat if the flashlight wasn't established — it is now (planted in the hero beat, used in the climax).
Too many 'then's. Dialogue should be shouted fragments, not sentences.
beat_map: Reveal every 10-15 s: step in dark (2s) → freeze (6s) → flicker jump-cuts (20s) → shadow hand (30s) → no-shadow ring (44s) → generator dies (52s) → flashlight (62s) → park (72s).

say: Keep the light on its face!
Behind its back, where the light couldn't reach…
It's moving in its own shadow!
Then light it from everywhere! Every car — circle it!
No front. No back. No shadows.
So Mia did what she'd done every night of her life.
One tiny light. Right in its eye.
They built a park around it. The lights there never go out.
And for the first time in her life…
Mia sleeps with the lights off.
